Definition: to attenuate, i.e. (figuratively) hide; a mystery
BiblicalUsage: Raz is a secret, a mystery — in Aramaic, the word for what is hidden and must be revealed. Daniel asked his companions to desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret, that they should not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon; then was the secret revealed unto Daniel in a night vision; and Daniel told the king, 'The secret which the king hath demanded cannot the wise men, the astrologers, the magicians, the soothsayers, shew unto the king; but there is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets.'
TheologicalSignificance: The lesson I take is that the secret is the gospel in miniature: no wise man can show it, and there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets — and He revealed this one to a young exile who prayed. And my position is that the mysteries of God are not locked away from His people; they are revealed to those who ask, in the night, on their knees.
